sent_to_model:
I'm replying to a guy on Reddit who's having no luck with women and seems pretty fixated on getting a girlfriend. Can you help me write a reply? I think that attitude could be putting people off, because nobody wants to feel interchangeable. I have a boyfriend myself, and being known as a person matters to me. I'd like to give this guy something useful about working on himself and finding people he actually connects with, including changing where he meets women and taking care of his appearance. He might also just struggle with conversation, so I want to give him a simple way to talk to someone when his mind goes blank. I'm happy to be blunt, but I do want to help. Please include widening his social circle, getting a friend to check an online dating profile if he uses one, and developing qualities he values in a partner. Most of this applies to women too.

- Replying to a man online about his lack of dating success.
- I have a boyfriend.
- /r/malefashionadvice is an available resource for men's clothing advice.
- The online community has resources for people dealing with social anxiety.
- Improving how you feel about your appearance can build confidence; confidence attracts women.
- Showing curiosity about someone makes conversation easier and helps them enjoy your company.
- Sexual attraction matters, but people also need to feel personally valued.
- Desperation puts potential partners off regardless of gender.
- His online manner seems desperate; if that carries over offline, it may explain his difficulties.
- For online dating, suggest getting a friend's feedback on his profile.
- Encourage a wider circle of friends and acquaintances.
- Suggest clothing advice and exercise where relevant.
- Make clear that most of this advice applies to women as well as men.
- Encourage him to develop qualities he would appreciate in a partner.
- Suggest different social settings if his current ones keep producing unsuitable matches: meetups instead of clubs.
- Suggest asking questions and following the answers when nervous, even if interest initially takes effort.

(About me: Reddit commenter in a relationship. Length: it should come to roughly 250-400 words.)

must_cover: Explain how desperation makes potential partners feel interchangeable, and that most of this advice applies to women as well as men.
Encourage developing qualities he would appreciate in a partner, changing where he meets people and widening his social circle.
If he dates online, suggest asking a friend to review his profile.
Suggest clothing advice and exercise where relevant, and explain how attention to appearance can improve confidence.
Suggest asking questions and following up on answers when nervous, showing interest even if it initially takes effort.

reference.kind: a real piece of writing by a real person

source.licence_note: CC BY 4.0 (dataset); posts by Reddit users
